section_summary: This section closes a 1938 agreement concerning International Standard Electric Corporation’s interests in Nippon Electric and Sumitomo, then records related share subscriptions, financing, and later stock agreements. It also contains company memoranda and historical agreements for radio and submarine cable services linking Japan with Peru and the United States, including rate schedules, operating terms, and reported wartime assets.

subfiles.title: Agreement among Sumitomo Honsha, Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works, and International Standard Electric Corporation, concluding page
subfiles.from: Sumitomo Honsha; Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works; International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: The concluding provisions govern arbitration and execution of the agreement.
subfiles.summary: Final arbitration clause, signatures, and Nippon Electric’s assent.

subfiles.title: Letter clarifying Article 12 share transfers
subfiles.from: Annis G. Jillard, International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: The parties clarify rights concerning transfers of substantial shareholdings.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies first purchase opportunity for large transfers and permits transfers within the Sumitomo Group.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning subscription rights in future stock issues
subfiles.from: Sumitomo Honsha and Sumitomo Electric Wire and Cable Works
subfiles.about: Sumitomo addresses International Standard Electric’s requested protections in future stock issues.
subfiles.summary: Sumitomo acknowledges desired proportional subscription rights but cannot guarantee them because Japanese practice reserves some new shares for premium sale.

subfiles.title: Subscription to new Nippon Electric shares
subfiles.from: International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: International Standard Electric elects to subscribe for part of its allotment of new shares.
subfiles.summary: Subscribes for 96,500 shares and surrenders rights to 65,993.5 shares to Sumitomo Honsha.

subfiles.title: Notice to Sumitomo Honsha of surrendered subscription rights
subfiles.from: International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: International Standard Electric sends Sumitomo a duplicate of its share subscription notice.
subfiles.summary: Confirms subscription for 96,500 shares and surrender of rights to 65,993.5 shares.

subfiles.title: Instructions for payment of ¥4,414,000 advance
subfiles.from: International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: International Standard Electric directs how the contractual advance should be disbursed.
subfiles.summary: Allocates the advance among a Nippon note, Sumitomo Electric shares, and an initial payment on new Nippon shares.

subfiles.title: Authorization to remit dividends and royalties to Sumitomo Honsha
subfiles.from: International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: Nippon Electric is instructed to direct later dividends and royalties toward repayment of an advance.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes payments to Sumitomo until ¥4,414,000 plus interest is repaid.

subfiles.title: Bond of debt for ¥4,414,000
subfiles.from: International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: The bond records repayment terms for the Sumitomo advance.
subfiles.summary: Promises repayment, with interest, from later Nippon Electric dividends and royalties.

subfiles.title: Minutes of extraordinary Nippon Electric shareholders meeting
subfiles.from: Nippon Electric Company, Limited
subfiles.about: Shareholders approve a capital increase, bylaw revisions, and new directors.
subfiles.summary: The meeting approves 350,000 new shares, raising capital to ¥30 million, revises articles governing directors and meetings, and elects M. Ogura, K. Ishikawa, T. Obata, and Sosthenes Behn.

subfiles.title: Agreement on Sumitomo and Nippon Electric share rights
subfiles.from: International Standard Electric Corporation and Sumitomo Honsha, Limited
subfiles.about: The parties arrange waived subscription rights, a possible share sale, and repurchase options.
subfiles.summary: International waives its rights to a Sumitomo Electric issue. Sumitomo agrees to buy 25,400 half-paid Nippon shares if called upon, enabling International to meet a capital call on its remaining shares. International receives a ten-year repurchase option and protection against losses from government interference.

subfiles.title: Clarification of October 1939 share agreement
subfiles.from: James E. Fullam, International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: The parties clarify subscription obligations, separate repurchase options, and share counts.
subfiles.summary: Adds Sumitomo’s obligation to buy waived shares, separates the two repurchase options, and corrects the Nippon half-paid share figures.

subfiles.title: Agreement substituting Sumitomo Electric Industries as purchaser of Nippon shares
subfiles.from: International Standard Electric Corporation; Sumitomo Honsha, Limited; Sumitomo Electric Industries, Limited
subfiles.about: Sumitomo Electric Industries assumes the purchase of 25,400 Nippon shares with a repurchase option for International.
subfiles.summary: Industries agrees to buy the shares for ¥1,778,000, allowing International to pay the call on its remaining shares. International retains a ten-year repurchase option; Industries protects associated rights, and Honsha guarantees its performance.

subfiles.title: Letter on future financing of Nippon and Sumitomo Electric
subfiles.from: James E. Fullam, International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: The parties set preferences for further financing of their jointly held companies.
subfiles.summary: Prefers nonconvertible debt for Sumitomo Electric and timed, fully paid share issues that International can fund from Japanese earnings.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning patent registration in Manchukuo
subfiles.from: James E. Fullam, International Standard Electric Corporation
subfiles.about: International permits Nippon to register patents in Manchukuo under defined conditions.
subfiles.summary: Patents may be registered in Nippon’s name at International’s expense and for its benefit. Nippon must assign them on request; registration does not enlarge its territorial rights under the 1926 agreement.

subfiles.title: All America Cables and Radio organization and Japan operations
subfiles.from: All America Cables and Radio, Inc.
subfiles.about: The memorandum describes the company, its Japan–Peru circuit, its closure, and wartime accounts.
subfiles.summary: Profiles officers and cable and radio operations. It summarizes the 1940 Tokyo–Lima radiotelegraph agreement, the circuit’s abandonment in 1942, $58,153.64 in recorded Japanese assets and receivables, and four attached documents.

subfiles.title: Japan–Peru duplex radiotelegraph agreement
subfiles.from: Department of Communications of Japan and All America Cables and Radio, Inc.
subfiles.about: The parties establish a duplex public radiotelegraph service between Japan and Peru.
subfiles.summary: Specifies stations, traffic, rates, government telegram discounts, accounting, emergency suspension, and a five-year initial term beginning July 1, 1940.

subfiles.title: Tokyo–Lima radio rate schedule
subfiles.from: Department of Communications of Japan and All America Cables and Radio, Inc.
subfiles.about: The schedule apportions per-word telegram rates across terminals, transit routes, and wireless transmission.
subfiles.summary: Lists ordinary, press, and some government rates for destinations in Central America, South America, and the West Indies, with shares allocated to Japan, Peru, onward carriage, transmission, and reception.

subfiles.title: Additional operating conditions for Tokyo–Lima circuit
subfiles.from: K. Tamura, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.to: C. C. Chapman, All America Cables and Radio, Inc.
subfiles.about: The parties confirm routing rules and technical requirements for the circuit.
subfiles.summary: Sets traffic routing exceptions and calls for equipment enabling 24-hour commercial operation.

subfiles.title: Letter concerning possible rate reductions
subfiles.from: K. Tamura, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.to: C. C. Chapman, All America Cables and Radio, Inc.
subfiles.about: The parties agree to discuss commercially practicable reductions in radiotelegraph rates.
subfiles.summary: Chapman confirms periodic consultation on rate reductions.

subfiles.title: Memorandum concerning Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.from: Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The memorandum reviews the company’s network, Japanese cable agreement, wartime assets, and attached agreements.
subfiles.summary: Describes the San Francisco–Shanghai cable route and its Bonin Islands connection to Japan. It recounts the 1905 Japanese agreement and its 1935 extension, including a 1939 State Department consultation. It reports $18,473.24 in Japanese assets and lists supporting agreements.

subfiles.title: Japan–Commercial Pacific Cable Company agreement
subfiles.from: Government of Japan and Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The parties establish and operate a Guam–Bonin Islands–Japan cable connection.
subfiles.summary: Allocates construction, landing rights, operation, traffic, revenue, repairs, and a thirty-year term.

subfiles.title: Additional arrangement on government telegrams
subfiles.from: Imperial Japanese Telegraph Administration and Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The parties set routing and discounted charges for Japanese and U.S. government telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Provides Pacific-route carriage, half-rate government charges, receiver-to-pay treatment, and termination terms.

subfiles.title: Understanding limiting two provisions of the 1906 arrangement
subfiles.from: Imperial Japanese Telegraph Administration and Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The parties exempt certain Japanese government telegrams from two routing provisions.
subfiles.summary: Excludes specified government telegrams and travelers’ messages from Articles I and II.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on cable traffic accounts
subfiles.from: Imperial Japanese Telegraph Administration and Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The parties prescribe accounting and settlement procedures for exchanged cable traffic.
subfiles.summary: Sets daily abstracts, monthly settlements, refunds, message markings, and English-language correspondence.

subfiles.title: 1935 additional Guam–Bonin cable agreement
subfiles.from: Department of Communications of Japan and Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The parties extend and modify the 1905 cable agreement.
subfiles.summary: Extends the agreement to thirty-five years, changes traffic obligations, waives the company electrician’s Peel Island placement, revises repairs, and applies international telecommunications rules.

subfiles.title: Letter voiding two articles of the 1906 arrangement
subfiles.from: S. Shindo, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.to: John Reifsnider, Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The parties confirm that two earlier routing provisions cease to apply.
subfiles.summary: Voids Articles I and II from September 12, 1935.

subfiles.title: Letter extending Bonin Islands traffic time
subfiles.from: S. Shindo, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.to: John Reifsnider, Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The parties confirm an additional daily period for Bonin Islands traffic.
subfiles.summary: Adds thirty minutes daily from 3:00 to 3:30 p.m. Japan time.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of U.S. State Department review period
subfiles.from: S. Shindo, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.to: John Reifsnider, Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The Japanese administration acknowledges submission of the agreement for U.S. review.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the State Department has thirty days after receipt to disapprove the agreement.

subfiles.title: Letter clarifying traffic under the proposed cable agreement
subfiles.from: N. Nagaoka, Chief of Foreign Telegraph Section
subfiles.to: John Reifsnider, Commercial Pacific Cable Company
subfiles.about: The Japanese administration clarifies routing of messages marked for the Bonin cable.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the company’s understanding of American traffic and Bonin routing, with a qualification that Japan cannot guarantee carriage beyond Nagasaki during cable interruptions. It says final approval and signing are expected soon.

subfiles.title: Mackay Radio and Telegraph Company organization and Japan operations
subfiles.from: Mackay Radio and Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: The memorandum describes Mackay’s business, Japan radio circuit, assets, and attached agreements.
subfiles.summary: Profiles officers, stations, and the San Francisco–Tokyo service under the 1934 agreement. It reports $137,645.62 in Japanese assets and receivables and lists five supporting documents.

subfiles.title: Japan–Mackay duplex radiotelegraph agreement
subfiles.from: Department of Communications of Japan and Mackay Radio and Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: The parties establish a duplex radiotelegraph service between Japan and the United States.
subfiles.summary: Sets station obligations, routing of Mackay and Japan-bound telegrams, rate components, equal sharing of radio charges, government-message discounts, accounting, and a five-year initial term from commercial opening.

subfiles.title: Letter on rates and a possible Japan–New York circuit
subfiles.from: N. Yamamoto, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.about: The parties agree to consider rate reductions and a direct Japan–New York circuit.
subfiles.summary: Chapman confirms consultation on rates and prompt consideration of a direct circuit.

subfiles.title: Letter on minimum traffic volume
subfiles.from: N. Yamamoto, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.about: Mackay agrees to seek a quarterly traffic volume comparable to a competing cable service.
subfiles.summary: Chapman confirms efforts to match Commercial Pacific’s corresponding U.S.–Japan message count.

subfiles.title: Letter on opening date for the radio circuit
subfiles.from: N. Yamamoto, Director General of Telecommunications
subfiles.about: The parties set a target and fallback date for commercial opening.
subfiles.summary: Targets October 1, 1934, with postponement for technical reasons no later than December 1.

subfiles.title: Supplemental radio traffic agreement, opening pages
subfiles.from: Department of Communications of Japan and Mackay Radio and Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: The parties begin amendments to the 1934 radio traffic agreement.
subfiles.summary: The opening clause adds an allocation of unrouted Japan-to-U.S. radio traffic to Mackay; the agreement continues beyond this section.
